applicable_when: The kernel is a small GEMM (M=2250, N=112, K=480) with a fixed tile configuration (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32, 128 threads/block). The 128 registers/thread is extremely high, limiting occupancy to 25% theoretical and only 6.25% achieved. The 12-way shared memory bank conflicts (77.63% of wavefronts) cause MIO stalls that dominate 65.6% of all stall cycles. With only 72 blocks for 132 SMs, most SMs are idle. Adding @triton.autotune with configurations that explore smaller BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N (to reduce register pressure and increase grid coverage), varied BLOCK_K, and different num_warps/num_stages will simultaneously address: (1) register pressure -> higher occupancy, (2) bank conflicts via different tile shapes, (3) grid coverage via more/smaller tiles, and (4) pipeline depth via num_stages for latency hiding.
